Investing.com - Futures linked to Canada's main stock index edged lower, as a surge in oil prices fueled concerns over energy-driven inflation, while worries swirled around the artificial intelligence trade following results from Meta Platforms.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

By 07:37 ET (11:37 GMT), the S&P/TSX 60 index standard futures contract had fallen by 13 points, or 0.6%.

On Wednesday, the S&P/TSX composite index finished higher by 0.6% at 36,324.99, notching its highest closing level since September 22.

Technology stocks advanced on strong quarterly results from SpaceX and Super Micro Computer, while a jump in Toronto-Dominion Bank powered a climb in heavily weighted financial stocks.

Meanwhile, Canada and the province of Ontario announced a new slate of measures aimed to buffer domestic steel and auto companies against the impact of U.S. tariffs.

U.S. futures slide

U.S. stock futures fell sharply, as investors parsed through earnings from Meta and Tesla. By 07:50 ET, the S&P 500 futures contract had fallen by 78 points, or 1.0%, Nasdaq 100 futures had dropped by 514 points, or 1.7%, and Dow futures had retreated by 298 points, or 0.6%.

The main averages on Wall Street advanced in the prior session, buoyed by strong results from Musk's rocket company SpaceX and server maker Super Micro Computer. The returns helped to assuage some recent concerns around the sustainability of the artificial intelligence trade, although analysts at Deutsche Bank flagged that the decline in Nasdaq futures could be a sign that not all investors were reassured.

Jitters have surrounded the AI sector for several days, triggered by a combination of heavy debt-fueled spending on AI infrastructure and elevated borrowing costs. Roller-coaster movements in AI-exposed stocks have mirrored shifting sentiment around AI, especially after fresh corporate returns appeared to indicate that demand for the nascent technology remains solid.

"When it comes to AI overall, it really does seem like the space has (permanently) entered a new era, one defined by less hospitable (or at the least more discerning) capital markets, which is why investors aren't as impressed as they were before by big headline spending numbers given the increased scrutiny on how the infrastructure will be paid for," analysts at Vital Knowledge said in a note.

The analysts also flagged worries that fighting between the U.S. and Iran could flare up once again in the coming weeks, possibly threatening oil supplies out of the Middle East in the process. Partially driving these fears was a New York Times report that the U.S. and Israel have drawn up plans for renewed strikes against Iran after the U.S. midterm elections in November, targeting Iran's energy infrastructure, nuclear facilities, and missile arsenal.

title: Does Super Micro's Big Quarter Make Nvidia Stock a Buy?
detail:
Does Super Micro's Big Quarter Make Nvidia Stock a Buy?
Daniel Sparks, The Motley Fool
Thu, October 22, 2026 at 12:32 AM MST 5 min read
SMCI
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ:SMCI) had a far bigger quarter than it expected. On Tuesday, the server builder said revenue for the first quarter of its fiscal 2027 (the period ended Sept. 30) should fall between $18.5 billion and $19.5 billion. In August, management had called for $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion.

At the midpoint of each range, the company's estimate was around $4 billion over what it expected. Super Micro said the gap was "primarily due to increased demand for AI platforms," and its shares popped about 9% on Wednesday as I write.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

For many investors, though, the more important stock here is Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA). Trading near $220 as I write this, the artificial intelligence (AI) chip leader is about 8% under $239.24, its record close, set on Oct. 6.

But does a server maker's surprise quarter make Nvidia stock a buy? I think it adds to a case that was already strong.

Image source: Getty Images.

Super Micro builds on Nvidia

Super Micro builds the servers and full racks that AI data centers run on. Its annual report for fiscal 2026 (the year ended June 30) puts Nvidia's Blackwell and Blackwell Ultra platforms first in its AI lineup.

It also says it expanded rack-scale manufacturing for Vera Rubin, Nvidia's next platform. And last November, Super Micro said its order book had over $13 billion in Blackwell Ultra orders.

Sure, Super Micro also sells systems built on rival chips, and it doesn't break out how much of its revenue runs on Nvidia hardware. Yet Nvidia's Blackwell systems seem to be what Super Micro leads with in AI.

Showing how fast that business has grown, the midpoint of Super Micro's new range (around $19 billion) is almost four times the $5.0 billion in revenue it posted in the year-ago quarter. It's also up around 71% from the $11.1 billion it reported in fiscal Q4 -- a quarter when sales almost doubled year over year.

The company now expects a gross margin (gross profit as a share of revenue) of 12% to 12.5%, over its 10.4% to 10.8% outlook and up from 9.3% the year before. It credited customer and product mix.

Keep in mind: these are preliminary, unaudited numbers. Super Micro will release its full results on Nov. 3.

What does it say about Nvidia's quarter?

Nvidia's fiscal third quarter started July 27, so August and September fall in both companies' quarters.

Nokia Oyj (HLSE:NOKIA) has pushed deeper into AI-native telecom infrastructure, announcing expanded work with NVIDIA, Supermicro, Cadence and operators like Elisa in the areas of AI-RAN, sovereign AI platforms and distributed edge computing.

Recent enthusiasm around AI-RAN and sovereign AI has not prevented short term volatility in Nokia Oyj. The share price is down 14.25% over the past 30 days and 5.38% over 90 days, even as the year-to-date share price return of 49.02% and 1-year total shareholder return of 77.54% indicate momentum that has been building over a longer horizon.

Scan beyond Nokia Oyj and see how other AI-infrastructure players are positioned by reviewing 55 AI infrastructure stocks in the same corner of the market.

Nokia Oyj now looks like a serious AI infrastructure platform, yet the share price has just stepped back sharply. Is the recent slide offering fair entry to that story, or is it already baking it in?

Most Popular Narrative: 46% Undervalued

Nokia Oyj closed at €8.23, while the most followed narrative, which applies a 7.68% discount rate, points to a fair value of €15.16. That gap has become a key reference point for investors trying to judge whether the latest price pullback is noise or something bigger.

Nokia delivered a strong second quarter, reporting revenue of €4.815 billion and earnings per share of €0.07, supported by growing demand for AI and cloud-related solutions. The company is also expanding its presence in the defense sector through AI-powered tools for 5G networks, creating additional opportunities to diversify revenue and strengthen long-term growth prospects.

See why 11 investors see Nokia Oyj as 46% undervalued.

According to TheTurntTomato, the narrative ties that earnings print and AI focus to a fair value of €15.16 for Nokia Oyj. The implied 46% discount to this estimate reflects an assumption that investors are heavily underpricing the role of AI-linked telecom and defense demand in Nokia Oyj's long term cash generation.

The same storyline leans on improving fundamentals already visible in the wider dataset. Annual revenue growth of 5.5%, net income growth of 31.33% per year on forecasts, and a move to profitability over the past five years all feed into that higher intrinsic value, even as current net profit margins sit at 3.4% compared to 5% a year earlier.

In addition, the narrative points to support from Nokia Oyj's balance sheet and capital position, such as €2.78b of cash reserves and a return profile that has outpaced both the Finnish market, up 15.9%, and the Finnish Communications industry, up 40.2%, over the past year. That mix of AI exposure, defense opportunities and historical total returns is a central part of why the popular thesis still sees room between price and value.

Super Micro Computer sharply lifted its preliminary fiscal Q1 2027 revenue outlook to US$18.5b to US$19.5b and raised expected gross margins to 12% to 12.5%, pointing to robust demand for its AI-focused infrastructure platforms.

The business is pairing this guidance shift with deeper ties to Nokia and Nutanix, signaling a push into AI-heavy 5G networks and enterprise AI factories. This could influence where Super Micro Computer earns its future infrastructure revenue.

Next, the focus turns to how Super Micro Computer's investment narrative lines up with this upgraded AI demand outlook and higher margin guidance.

Scan how Super Micro Computer's AI momentum compares with other infrastructure plays by reviewing the hand-picked 55 AI infrastructure stocks powering data centers and edge networks.

What Is Super Micro Computer's Investment Narrative?

To own Super Micro Computer, you need to be comfortable with a story built on heavy AI infrastructure demand, high capital needs, and tight execution. The Nokia AI RAN deal and Nutanix alliances slot directly into that thesis. They point to Super Micro Computer hardware being baked into telecom edge networks and enterprise AI factories, not just hyperscale data centers. The upgraded revenue and margin outlook suggests current demand is strong, but it also raises the bar for what counts as a positive surprise in coming quarters.

The nearer term swing factors look very operational. Management has to source GPUs and new NVIDIA Vera CPUs at scale, build and ship complex racks like the Vera CPU systems, and still keep gross margin around the guided 12% to 12.5% while funding growth from higher risk, mostly debt based liabilities. New leadership in the CFO seat and a fresh AI heavy board appointment show the organisation is being tuned for this phase. The pay-off depends on whether these AI partnerships translate into recurring, higher quality earnings rather than one off build outs.
